info.title: HourSquare Public API
info.description:
The HourSquare public API: record clock events and completed shifts, read time entries, and list employees for one company.

**Authentication.** Create an API key in HourSquare (Settings → API & integrations; you see it once). Exchange it for an access token at `https://api.hoursquare.com/api/public/v1/oauth/token` (OAuth 2.0 client credentials: `grant_type=client_credentials`, the key as `client_secret` or as the HTTP Basic password). Send the token as `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`. **Tokens live 15 minutes** — cache one and request a new one when it expires or on a 401. Never put a key or a token in a URL.

**Scopes.** A key carries the scopes it was created with; each operation below names the one it needs (`attendance.record`, `attendance.read`, `employees.read`, …). A person's own HourSquare token may also call the operations their permissions cover. Calling without the scope returns `403 insufficient_scope`. When fetched with a token, this document lists only the operations that token may call.

**Rate limits.** 300 requests per minute per key on these resources and 60 per minute per key on the token endpoint, sliding windows, enforced per server instance (so approximately). Every response carries `RateLimit`, `RateLimit-Policy` and `X-RateLimit-Limit` / `X-RateLimit-Remaining` / `X-RateLimit-Reset`; a `429 rate_limited` carries `Retry-After`.

**Revocation.** Revoking a key stops new tokens immediately; tokens already issued keep working until they expire, so **within 15 minutes of Revoke every request with that key fails**.

**Errors.** Every error is `application/problem+json` (RFC 9457) with a stable snake_case `error` you can branch on (`employee_not_found`, `already_clocked_in`, `no_open_session`, `session_too_long`, `overlaps_existing_entry`, `day_locked`, `validation_failed`, `idempotency_key_reused`, `time_tracking_disabled`, `insufficient_scope`, `rate_limited`, …), the numeric `code`, a human `detail`, and a `correlationId` to quote to support. `validation_failed` (422) lists the offending fields in `errors[]`.

**Idempotency.** Send an `Idempotency-Key` header (unique per request, at most 128 characters) on writes to make retries safe: the same key replays the first response. Without it, the same employee, event type and caller within 60 seconds of an existing entry returns that entry with `200` instead of a duplicate; a later retry may see `409` instead of the original `201`.

**Dry run.** `X-HourSquare-Dry-Run: true` on any write validates and resolves everything, writes nothing, and returns the would-be result with `dryRun: true` and status 200. This document declares the header with default `true`, so a try-it panel never writes unless you flip it; the server treats an absent header as a real write.

**Time zones.** `occurredAt`, `clockIn` and `clockOut` are RFC 3339 timestamps with an explicit offset. They are recorded in the employee's workplace time zone, else the company's; when neither is configured the wall-clock you sent is kept. The response echoes `timeZone` (an IANA id or `offset`) and the server-resolved instant.

**Versioning.** The major version is in the path (`/api/public/v1`). Within v1 only additive changes happen: new optional fields, new endpoints, new enum values (documented as "may grow"). Breaking changes get `/v2`; v1 then carries `Deprecation` and `Sunset` headers for at least six months.

**Keep it safe.** Keys and tokens never belong in a URL, a browser page or a log; rotate a key when in doubt (the old one keeps working for the grace period you choose).

get.description:
The company's employees (never deleted ones) with the fields an integrator needs to build its badge map:
id, external id, name, e-mail, employment status, department and position ids. Ordered by id; pass
`nextCursor` back as `cursor` while `hasMore` is true.

Requires scope `employees.read` (52).

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only employees with this employment status: `active`, `inactive`, `on_leave`, `suspended`, `terminated`.

401.description: The bearer token is missing, invalid or expired (`invalid_token`). Request a new token from the token endpoint.

403.description: The token does not carry the required scope (`insufficient_scope`), or time tracking is switched off for the company (`time_tracking_disabled`).

422.description: The request itself is wrong (`validation_failed`, with one `errors[]` item per field; or `idempotency_key_reused`).

429.description: Rate limit exceeded (`rate_limited`): 300 requests per minute per key on this surface, approximately (per pod). Honour `Retry-After` and the `RateLimit` headers.

put.description:
Sets (or, with a null / blank value, clears) the badge / HRIS id this employee is matched by in
`employee.externalId`. At most 64 characters, compared exactly as sent (case-sensitive), unique inside
your company: a value another employee already carries returns `409 already_exists` naming them.
`X-HourSquare-Dry-Run: true` checks the value without writing.

Requires scope `attendance.record` (86).

parameters.description: Validate without writing: every check and resolution runs, nothing is stored, and the response carries `dryRun: true` with status 200. Send `false` (or omit the header) to write for real.

`hsq_` public id), the company it belongs to, the scopes it may use, when it expires, and the quota
it is charged against (`requestsPerMinute`, per pod — so "approximately"). No scope required.

post.description:
Records a `clock_in`, `clock_out` or `toggle` punch for one employee of your company, identified by
`employee.id` and/or `employee.externalId`.
            
* `occurredAt` is RFC 3339 **with an offset** (`2026-09-14T08:59:12+04:00`), at most 5 minutes in the
  future (clock skew) and 30 days in the past. It is converted into the employee's workplace time zone
  (else the company's); when neither is configured the wall-clock you sent is kept. The response echoes
  which (`timeZone`: an IANA id or `offset`) and the server-resolved `occurredAt`.
* `clock_in` opens a session; `clock_out` completes the open session of that day (or the previous day's
  still-open one — an overnight shift stays one entry on the day it started, `endsNextDay: true`) and
  submits it for approval; `toggle` picks whichever applies and is the recommended type for dumb clocks.
* Sessions of 24 hours or more are refused (`session_too_long`); record such shifts with `POST /time-entries`.
* Send an `Idempotency-Key` to make retries safe. Without it, the same employee, type and caller
  within 60 seconds of an existing entry returns that entry with `200` instead of creating a duplicate.
* `X-HourSquare-Dry-Run: true` runs every check and resolution, writes nothing and returns the would-be
  result with `dryRun: true` and status `200`.

Requires scope `attendance.record` (86).

parameters.name: X-HourSquare-Dry-Run
parameters.description: Validate without writing: every check and resolution runs, nothing is stored, and the response carries `dryRun: true` with status 200. Send `false` (or omit the header) to write for real.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Optional, recommended. A unique key (at most 128 characters, e.g. a UUID) that makes a retry safe: the same key with the same body replays the first response verbatim (with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`), the same key with a different body is refused (`422 idempotency_key_reused`), and a key whose first request is still running answers `409 idempotency_in_flight`. Keys are kept for 24 hours.

post.description:
Records a shift that is already over — including an overnight one — as one time entry on the day it
started, and submits it for approval exactly like a shift logged in HourSquare.
            
* `clockIn` and `clockOut` are RFC 3339 **with an offset**; `clockOut` must be after `clockIn` and less
  than 24 hours later; `clockIn` at most 30 days in the past, `clockOut` at most 5 minutes in the future.
* The same time-zone rule as clock events applies (workplace zone, else company zone, else the wall-clock
  you sent); `timeZone` in the response says which.
* `breakMinutes` is recorded as one unpaid break in the middle of the shift. Not allowed on an overnight shift.
* `Idempotency-Key` makes retries safe; `X-HourSquare-Dry-Run: true` validates without writing.

Requires scope `attendance.record` (86).

get.description:
Exactly one of `employeeId` / `externalId` selects the employee. `from` and `to` are inclusive work
dates (`YYYY-MM-DD`) spanning at most 92 days; by default the last 30 days. Ordered by work date, then id;
pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor` while `hasMore` is true.

Requires scope `attendance.read` (47).

parameters.name: employeeId
parameters.description: The employee's HourSquare id (send this or `externalId`).

parameters.name: externalId
parameters.description: The employee's external id (send this or `employeeId`).

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: First work date, inclusive. Default: `to` minus 30 days.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Last work date, inclusive. Default: today.

post.summary: Exchange an API key for an access token.
post.description: OAuth 2.0 client credentials (RFC 6749 §4.4). Send `grant_type=client_credentials` as `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` and the key either as the `client_secret` field or as the HTTP Basic password (`Authorization: Basic base64(hsq_xxxxxxxx:<key>)`). The token lives 15 minutes (`expires_in`, seconds): cache it and request a new one when it elapses or on a 401. This endpoint is served by the identity service under the same host; it allows 60 requests per minute per key. Every response is `Cache-Control: no-store`.

client_id.description: Optional. The key's public id, with or without the `hsq_` prefix. When present it must match the key.

client_secret.description: The whole key (`hsq_…`). Omit it when the key travels as the HTTP Basic password instead. Never send it in the query string.

400.description: `invalid_request` (unreadable body, a secret in the query string, two authentication mechanisms, a repeated parameter) or `unsupported_grant_type` (anything but `client_credentials`).

401.description: `invalid_client`: unknown key, wrong secret, or a key that is revoked, expired, outside its IP allowlist, or whose company has API access switched off (`error_description` says which once possession is proved).

ProblemDetails.description:
The wire shape. Code is the numeric ApiExceptionCodeTypes value,
            Error the stable snake_case string integrators branch on.

externalId.description: The badge / HRIS id to match this employee by (at most 64 characters, case-sensitive, unique per company). Null or blank clears it.

TimeEntryWriteResponse.description:
The 201 (200 for a dry run or a header-less dedupe hit) body of POST /time-clock/events and
POST /time-entries (plan §6). type is the EFFECTIVE type (toggle resolves to
clock_in or clock_out; a completed shift is shift). workDate / time
are the entry's stored wall-clock values in timeZone (an IANA id, or offset when the
sent offset was kept), and occurredAt is the server-resolved instant. endsNextDay is true
for an overnight shift (the entry stays on the day it started). timeEntryId is null on a
dry-run clock-in (nothing was created).

EmployeeRef.description: Every public response that names an employee carries this pair.

TimeClockEventRequest.description: Body of POST /api/public/v1/time-clock/events — a live punch (plan §6).

employee.description: The employee, by HourSquare id and/or external id. At least one is required; both must match when both are sent.

type.description: clock_in, clock_out or toggle (open session for that day exists ? clock_out : clock_in — the recommended type for dumb clocks).

occurredAt.description: When the punch happened: RFC 3339 with an explicit offset (2026-09-14T08:59:12+04:00). At most 5 minutes in the future and 30 days in the past.

deviceId.description: Optional identifier of the device or bridge that sent the punch (at most 64 characters). Stored on the entry's notes as [device: …].

note.description: Optional note for the manager (at most 500 characters).

EmployeeSelector.description:
How a public request names an employee (company API keys plan 2026-09-15, §6 "Employee
identification"): by HourSquare id, by the external (badge / HRIS) id, or both — every supplied
selector must match, and both are resolved inside the caller's company only.

externalId.description: The external id set through the Hub or PUT /employees/{id}/external-id (case-sensitive, at most 64 characters).

TimeClockEventType.description:
The type of a time-clock event (plan §6). toggle is the recommended type for
            dumb clocks: open session on that day (or the previous day) exists ? clock_out : clock_in.

CreateTimeEntryRequest.description: Body of POST /api/public/v1/time-entries — a completed shift, including overnight (plan §6).

employee.description: The employee, by HourSquare id and/or external id.

clockIn.description: When the shift started: RFC 3339 with an explicit offset. At most 30 days in the past.

clockOut.description: When the shift ended: RFC 3339 with an explicit offset, after clockIn and less than 24 hours later. At most 5 minutes in the future.

breakMinutes.description: Unpaid break in minutes, recorded as one break in the middle of the shift. Not allowed on an overnight shift.

note.description: Optional note for the manager (at most 500 characters).

OAuthTokenResponse.description: RFC 6749 §5.1 token response, as Identity's token endpoint returns it (documentation-only type).

OAuth2.description: Client credentials (RFC 6749 §4.4): POST your API key as `client_secret` (or as the HTTP Basic password) to the token URL and use the returned token as a Bearer. Tokens live 15 minutes. Each operation lists the scope it requires; a key carries the scopes it was created with.

scopes.attendance.record: Record clock events and completed shifts; set employee external ids (permission 86)
scopes.employees.read: Read employees (id, external id, name, email, status) (permission 52)

BearerToken.description: An access token from the token endpoint (`Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`), or a person's own HourSquare session token: a person may call the read operations their permissions cover.
